# Gantt Phase 1A — Implementation Plan

## Context

Build a local-only CLI that renders an HTML Gantt chart for any Runway L1 project or wrapper retainer, and surfaces data-quality gaps inline (per row) and at the top (chart-level alerts). Goal: give Jason a fast, repeatable way to see what's missing in Runway data so he can drive cleanup. AG1 is the worst-case primary fixture (lots of nulls).

Phase 1A is HTML-only (no PNG, no Slack, no deploy). Phase 1B adds Slack wiring; Phase 2 adds PNG rendering + brand polish. The deterministic-template choice (a single `.tsx` component) keeps Phase 1B and the R2 brand pass cheap — they just reuse this component.

Branch: `feature/gantt-cli`. Worktree: `.worktrees/gantt-cli/`. Long-running local feature branch — no PR until operator approves.

Spec sources (treat as canonical):
- `docs/tmp/gantt-phase-1-pre-plan.md` — full scope, locked decisions, alert taxonomy, wave decomposition
- `docs/tmp/gantt-phase-1-cc-handoff.md` — workflow, stop conditions, mechanical checks per wave

## Constraints (operator-locked, do not relitigate)

- Render template as a React `.tsx` component → HTML via `renderToStaticMarkup` from `react-dom/server`
- Issue detection is deterministic and pure (no LLM)
- Implement only the rules in pre-plan §5 — do not invent additional rules or "section groupings"
- Sort children by `startDate` (nulls last). Title rendered verbatim from DB
- Header date range shows raw L1/wrapper dates — including `null – null` if both are null. Do NOT derive from children
- Output: `~/runway-gantts/[client-slug]-[project-slug]-[YYYY-MM-DD].html`
- Wrapper detection: ALL of (`parentProjectId === null`) AND (`engagementType === "retainer"`) AND (has ≥1 child via `parentProjectId`)
- L2 input → error: `"'X' is a child project. Did you mean its parent 'Y'?"`
- Stop and report after each wave. Do not push, open a PR, or run preflight/code-review/pr-ready/atomic-commits without operator approval.

## Reusable infrastructure (do not reimplement)

- DB connection: `createRunwayDb()` from `scripts/lib/run-script.ts` — wraps `RUNWAY_DATABASE_URL` + libsql + drizzle
- Env loading: `loadEnvLocal()` (already auto-runs on import of `run-script.ts`)
- Direct-execution guard: `runIfDirect(name, fn)` from `scripts/lib/run-script.ts`
- Fuzzy match: `fuzzyMatch<T>` and `resolveEntityOrFail<T>` in `src/lib/runway/operations-utils.ts:189-276` — exact → startsWith → substring with ambiguity reporting. Reuse for project name resolution
- Project schema: `projects` table in `src/lib/db/runway-schema.ts:26-59`. Key fields: `name`, `clientId`, `status`, `category`, `owner`, `resources`, `waitingOn`, `dueDate`, `startDate`, `endDate`, `contractStart`, `contractEnd`, `engagementType`, `parentProjectId`
- Vitest config: `vitest.config.mts` — `happy-dom`, `@vitejs/plugin-react`, includes `**/*.test.{ts,tsx}`. `.tsx` test files supported

Slugify helper does not exist as exported util. Inline a 5-line one (`toLowerCase`, replace `[^a-z0-9]+` with `-`, strip leading/trailing `-`).

`react`/`react-dom` 19.2.3 already in `package.json` — no new deps.

## Files to create

```
scripts/
  runway-gantt.tsx                      # CLI entry point
  runway-gantt.test.ts                  # CLI-level tests (arg parsing, output path)
  lib/gantt/
    types.ts                            # GanttRow, GanttData, IssueCode, etc.
    types.test.ts                       # type-shape sanity (or co-located)
    resolve-entity.ts                   # fuzzy project resolution + wrapper detection
    resolve-entity.test.ts
    extract-data.ts                     # DB queries: project + children
    extract-data.test.ts
    transform-rows.ts                   # map children → GanttRow, sort, axis params
    transform-rows.test.ts
    detect-issues.ts                    # L1, wrapper, L2 issue detection (pure)
    detect-issues.test.ts
    counter.ts                          # top-of-chart counter + console mirror formatter
    counter.test.ts
    GanttTemplate.tsx                   # React component (header + alerts + body)
    GanttTemplate.test.tsx              # renderToStaticMarkup snapshot/structure tests
```

Rationale for splitting under `scripts/lib/gantt/`: keeps the CLI script thin, lets each pure module be unit-tested in isolation, mirrors the `src/lib/runway/operations-*` layout convention. All modules are `.ts` except the React component and the CLI entry (which contains JSX) — the CLI is `.tsx` per pre-plan §1 and the Turbopack `.tsx`-for-JSX gotcha in `.claude/MEMORY.md`.

## Pre-work (before Wave 1)

Add npm script to `package.json`:
```json
"runway:gantt": "npx tsx scripts/runway-gantt.tsx"
```

`scripts/lib/run-script.ts` already calls `loadEnvLocal()` on import, so this single-line script wires env via the same path as `runway:migrate` / `runway:publish-updates`. (Their package.json entries are also bare `npx tsx` — env loading happens inside the script via the shared lib.)

## Wave 1 — Entity resolution

**Deliverable:** `scripts/lib/gantt/resolve-entity.ts` + tests.

**Behavior:**
1. Input: project name string OR project id
2. If input matches a project id (exact `id` match) → return that project. Otherwise treat as name and pull all projects from DB, run `fuzzyMatch` over `(client.name + " / " + project.name)` AND over project.name alone — match union. Disambiguation: if multiple, error with the list of candidates as `"<Client>: <Project Name>"`.
3. After resolving, classify:
   - `parentProjectId !== null` → return `{ kind: "l2-error", message: "'<name>' is a child project. Did you mean its parent '<parentName>'?" }`
   - `parentProjectId === null && engagementType === "retainer" && children.length > 0` → `{ kind: "wrapper", project, children }`
   - Otherwise → `{ kind: "l1", project }` (children fetched in Wave 2)
4. Children are pulled via a single `WHERE parent_project_id = ?` query and reused downstream.

**Tests:** ambiguous-name disambiguation, L2-input error message, wrapper detection (all 3 conditions individually flipped), retainer-with-no-children falls through to L1, id-input bypasses fuzzy match.

**Mechanical checks:** `pnpm test:run`, `pnpm lint`. Run the resolver against the live local DB for `"AG1"`, `"Social Content Trial"`, `"HDL Website Build"`, `"Convergix"` and confirm classifications.

## Wave 2 — Data extraction

**Deliverable:** `scripts/lib/gantt/extract-data.ts` + tests.

**Behavior:**
1. For an L1 view: pull all `weekItems` and L2 `projects` whose `parentProjectId === project.id`. Pre-plan §5 frames "child rows" as the next layer of detail under L1 — for a normal L1 with no L2 children this means weekItems; for a wrapper-style L1 it means child L1 projects. **Open question for operator: does a "normal L1" Gantt show weekItems as children, or only L2 projects?** Default assumption (reflected in the plan): a normal L1 shows its **L2 projects** as children (`parents.parentProjectId = L1.id`). WeekItems are out of scope for Phase 1A — they are operational granularity, not L1 schedule structure. If operator confirms otherwise, this wave changes; everything downstream still works because the row shape is identical.
2. For a wrapper view: children are the L1 projects with `parentProjectId === wrapper.id` (already fetched in Wave 1).
3. Look up the client row (for `client.name` and `client.slug` used in header + filename).
4. Return a `RawData` shape: `{ kind, entity, client, children }` — children typed as `Project[]`.

**Tests:** L1 with 0 children, L1 with N L2 children, wrapper with N child L1s, batch-fetch query shape (single `inArray` not N+1).

**Mechanical checks:** lint + tests + live-DB run on AG1 (expect wrapper + N children) and Soundly Payment Gateway (expect L1).

## Wave 3 — Row transformation + axis params

**Deliverable:** `scripts/lib/gantt/transform-rows.ts` + tests.

**Behavior:**
1. Map each child to `GanttRow`: `{ id, title, owner, resources, startDate, endDate, status, category, engagementType, parentProjectId, dueDate, waitingOn, contractStart, contractEnd }`. **Issues are populated in Wave 4, not here** — keep transform pure.
2. Sort by `startDate` ascending, **nulls last** (use a comparator that treats `null` as `+Infinity`).
3. Compute axis params: collect non-null start/end across rows + entity; if all null → `{ kind: "no-axis" }`; if span < 16 weeks → `{ kind: "weekly", start, end, weekColumns: [...] }`; else `{ kind: "monthly", start, end, monthColumns: [...] }`. "Today" line: pass through `today: ISOString` so callers can place it deterministically.
4. Date-range header value: `formatHeaderRange(entity.startDate, entity.endDate)` — `null – null` if both null, `Apr 17 – May 11` otherwise. Use a tiny formatter (no date-fns dep yet — `Date` + `toLocaleDateString("en-US", { month: "short", day: "numeric" })` is enough).

**Tests:** sort with mixed nulls, weekly vs monthly threshold (15 weeks → weekly, 17 weeks → monthly, 16 weeks boundary), all-null axis returns `no-axis`, header-range formatter for all 4 null permutations + same-day milestone.

**Mechanical checks:** lint + tests.

## Wave 4 — Issue detection (deterministic)

**Deliverable:** `scripts/lib/gantt/detect-issues.ts` + tests. Pure functions. No DB, no I/O.

**Implementation:** one detector per scope, returning `Issue[]` where `Issue = { code: IssueCode; message: string }`.

`IssueCode` enum (string union):
- L1: `l1-null-dates`, `l1-retainer-null-contract`, `l1-null-engagement-type`, `l1-null-category-or-status`, `l1-awaiting-null-waiting-on`, `l1-due-end-mismatch`, `l1-no-children-no-owner`
- Wrapper: `wrapper-null-contract`, `wrapper-no-children`, `wrapper-range-misses-children`, `wrapper-bad-engagement-type`, `wrapper-child-contract-mismatch`
- L2/child row: `child-active-null-owner`, `child-orphan`, `child-parent-date-mismatch`, `child-end-before-start`, `child-status-category-mismatch`, `child-awaiting-null-waiting-on`, `child-null-engagement-when-parent-set`
- Date-row issues (visualized in the row itself, not in sub-row): `row-both-dates-null`, `row-only-start-null`, `row-only-end-null`, `row-end-before-start`

**Critical mapping** (per pre-plan §5 "L2 alert sub-row"): row-date issues are NOT shown as sub-row alerts — they are visualized inline (`null – null`, no bar, etc.). Sub-row only fires on issues BEYOND date issues. The detector returns separate arrays: `dateIssues[]` (rendered inline in the row) and `subRowIssues[]` (rendered in alert sub-row). Same for L1/wrapper level: chart-top alerts vs row-level alerts are separated.

**Tests:** one test per issue code (positive case fires; negative case does not), plus combined cases (e.g., L2 with both end<start AND null owner → date issue + sub-row issue), plus the exact wording check for "is retainer but" / "doesn't cover all child date ranges" so they match the spec. Use small factory helpers (`makeProject({ overrides })`) per `CLAUDE.md` testing pattern.

**Mechanical checks:** lint + tests. Live-DB sanity check: run detector against AG1 wrapper + AG1 children + AG1 "Social Content Trial" and confirm the expected codes fire.

**Stop condition:** if a real record fires a rule that the operator says is wrong, stop and report — could be a rule to revise OR a real data issue.

## Wave 5 — React template

**Deliverable:** `scripts/lib/gantt/GanttTemplate.tsx` + tests.

**Component shape:** `<GanttTemplate data={GanttData} />` returning the full `<html><head>...</head><body>...</body></html>` document with inline CSS in a `<style>` tag (no external assets — file must render standalone in any browser).

**Sections:**
1. **Header**: project/wrapper name, raw date range, "Generated YYYY-MM-DD", legend
2. **Top-of-chart counter**: "X of Y rows have data gaps" + itemized list grouped by issue code (deferred to Wave 6 but stub the slot here)
3. **Alert section** (above body): chart-level L1 OR wrapper alerts — render only if non-empty
4. **Gantt body** (table layout, not SVG for Phase 1A — simpler, more debuggable):
   - Each row is a flex/grid line: title • owner+resources (`O: <owner> · CD: Lane, CW: Kathy`) • inline dates • bar/marker
   - Bar is a positioned div with `left/width` computed from axis params
   - Milestone (start === end) → diamond glyph (CSS `::before` rotated square)
   - "Today" vertical line is a single absolutely-positioned div
   - Sub-row appears beneath the row when `subRowIssues.length > 0` — small, indented, alert-colored
5. **All-null axis path**: when `axis.kind === "no-axis"`, omit the timeline column; rows still render with their inline `null – null`

**Styling:** Phase 1A is functional, not branded. Use a neutral palette (greys + accent for active, red for alerts). Inline CSS only. Brand polish is R2.

**HTML render entry:** `renderGantt(data: GanttData): string` → `"<!doctype html>" + renderToStaticMarkup(<GanttTemplate data={data} />)`.

**Tests:** structural assertions on rendered HTML (using `happy-dom` via vitest — parse the string back via `DOMParser` or substring assertions). Validate: header text, row count matches input, milestone diamond present for same-day rows, no bar element when both dates null, sub-row only present when expected, "Today" line rendered when axis is not `no-axis`.

**Mechanical checks:** lint + tests. **Visual check: open the rendered HTML in a browser** before declaring the wave done (handoff requirement). Use `open ~/runway-gantts/<file>.html` on macOS.

## Wave 6 — Top-of-chart counter + console mirror

**Deliverable:** `scripts/lib/gantt/counter.ts` + tests.

**Behavior:**
1. `summarize(data: GanttData): Summary` → `{ rowsWithGaps: number; totalRows: number; byCode: Record<IssueCode, RowRef[]> }`. Group every per-row issue and chart-level issue by code, listing affected entities.
2. `formatCounterMarkup(summary)`: returns JSX for the top-of-chart slot. Format: headline + list grouped by code with friendly labels (e.g., `"3 children missing end date: A, B, C"`).
3. `formatCounterConsole(summary)`: returns a plain-text version for stdout. Same data, no markup.
4. Wave 5's `GanttTemplate` consumes `formatCounterMarkup(summary)`. CLI in Wave 7 consumes `formatCounterConsole(summary)`.

**Tests:** zero issues → "0 of N rows have data gaps", grouping logic with multiple codes, deterministic ordering (sort by code name for stability).

**Mechanical checks:** lint + tests.

## Wave 7 — CLI wrapper

**Deliverable:** `scripts/runway-gantt.tsx` + `scripts/runway-gantt.test.ts`.

**Behavior:**
1. Args: `--project <name|id>`. No other flags in Phase 1A.
2. Validate args → on missing/invalid, print usage to stderr and `process.exit(1)`.
3. Pipeline: `resolveEntity` → on `l2-error`, print message + exit 1; on success → `extractData` → `transformRows` → `detectIssues` → `summarize` → `renderGantt`.
4. Resolve output path: `path.join(os.homedir(), "runway-gantts", `${slugify(client.name)}-${slugify(project.name)}-${YYYY-MM-DD}.html`)`. `mkdirSync(dir, { recursive: true })`. `writeFileSync(path, html, "utf-8")`.
5. Print to stdout: console-mirror counter, then `Wrote: <absolute path>`.
6. Errors: wrap pipeline in try/catch, print friendly message + exit 1. Turso connection errors get a hint about `RUNWAY_DATABASE_URL`.

**Tests:** arg parsing (missing `--project`, valid `--project`, multiple values), output-path derivation (slug correctness for various names with punctuation/spaces), error-message wording for L2 input.

**Mechanical checks:** lint + tests. **End-to-end smoke**: `pnpm runway:gantt --project "AG1"` → file exists at expected path, opens in browser, header reads "AG1" + raw date range, all expected children present.

## Wave 8 — Cross-project validation

**Deliverable:** validation report (notes back to operator, not a committed file). Iterate template + thresholds based on what we see.

**Required runs:**
- AG1 (wrapper, worst-case)
- AG1 → "Social Content Trial" (L1 with placeholder same-day L2 dates — verify milestone glyph)
- HDL Website Build (good data, normal L1)
- Convergix (wrapper, large)
- Soundly Payment Gateway (medium L1)
- One degenerate case: an L1 with no children (find one in DB or pick any with empty children — we expect "no children" alert for the L1 case)
- One L2-input case (any L2): confirm error message wording

**For each:** open rendered HTML in browser. Capture observations against the spec — does anything look wrong? Did a rule fire on something it shouldn't have? Are alert thresholds reasonable? Bring observations back to operator before any spec/threshold change.

**Tests woven in:** add fixture-based test cases to `detect-issues.test.ts` derived from any genuine surprises uncovered.

**Mechanical checks:** all of `pnpm test:run`, `pnpm lint` green at the end. Operator review gate before any commit. No PR.

## Verification (end-to-end)

After Wave 7, before Wave 8:
1. `pnpm test:run` — all green
2. `pnpm lint` — zero errors
3. `pnpm runway:gantt --project "AG1"` — exits 0, writes file, prints absolute path
4. `open ~/runway-gantts/ag1-ag1-2026-04-28.html` (or whatever path is printed) — file renders, header correct, alerts populated, rows visible, "Today" line drawn
5. `pnpm runway:gantt --project "AG1 Social Drafts"` (an L2) — exits 1 with the disambiguation message

After Wave 8: 6 cross-project runs all render correctly per spec. Operator has reviewed at least 2 outputs visually.

## Stop conditions (per handoff)

Pause and report to operator on any of:
- Pre-plan ambiguity surfaces during implementation
- A data-quality rule fires on a record that "looks fine" — could be rule revision OR real issue
- AG1 (or any test fixture) renders something that looks wrong
- Turso/env/connection issues block reading data
- Each wave completion (built-in checkpoint)

## Out of scope (do not drift)

- PNG / Playwright rendering (Phase 2)
- Slack triggering (Phase 1B)
- Brand polish (R2 — Civilization colors/fonts/logo header)
- Caching / memoization
- Output destination beyond `~/runway-gantts/` (Phase 2 may move to Google Drive)
- Hosted live URL (Phase 2)
- Multi-format bundle, AI-generated summary text
- Modifying project titles for display, deriving header dates from children, inventing sections from data

## Open questions for operator before build starts

1. **Children of a normal L1**: confirm Phase 1A renders **L2 projects** (`parentProjectId = L1.id`) as the child rows for a normal L1, and weekItems are out of scope. (My read of pre-plan §5 says yes — please confirm.)
2. **L1 with no children alert**: pre-plan §5 says "L1 has no children AND no owner" is the alert condition. So an L1 with no children but WITH an owner gets no alert. Is that the intended threshold?

# Gantt Phase 1A — Implementation Plan (v2, operator-corrected)

## Context

Build a local-only CLI that renders an HTML Gantt chart for any Runway project (wrapper, top-level L1, or sub-project) and surfaces data-quality gaps inline (per row) and at the top (chart-level). Goal: give Jason a fast, repeatable way to see what's missing in Runway data so he can drive cleanup. AG1 is the worst-case primary fixture.

Phase 1A is HTML-only. Phase 1B = Slack wiring. Phase 2 = PNG + brand polish. The deterministic-template choice (a single `.tsx` component) keeps Phase 1B and the R2 brand pass cheap.

Branch: `feature/gantt-cli`. Worktree: `.worktrees/gantt-cli/`. Long-running local feature branch — no PR, preflight, code-review, pr-ready, or atomic-commits without explicit operator approval.

Spec sources: `docs/tmp/gantt-phase-1-cc-handoff.md` (workflow) and `docs/tmp/gantt-phase-1-pre-plan.md` (scope, alert taxonomy). **This plan is canonical for the build.** TP will update the pre-plan separately to reflect operator corrections — do not edit it.

## Data model (operator-verified)

- **L1** = a row in `projects` (top-level OR with `parentProjectId` pointing at a retainer wrapper)
- **L2** = a row in `weekItems` (always)
- **Wrapper** = an L1 with `parentProjectId === null` AND `engagementType === "retainer"` AND ≥1 child L1 (`projects.parentProjectId === wrapper.id`)
- A non-retainer L1's only children are **weekItems**
- Sub-projects only exist under retainer wrappers (validator-enforced)

### Chart-subject classification

After resolving an entity:
- `parentProjectId === null && engagementType === "retainer" && childProjects.length > 0` → **wrapper view** (children = child L1 projects)
- All other cases → **L1 view** (children = weekItems WHERE `projectId === entity.id`). This includes:
  - Top-level non-retainer L1
  - Sub-project (`parentProjectId !== null`) — renders normally with its own weekItems
  - Degenerate retainer with no child projects

Sub-projects are valid Gantt subjects. **Drop the prior "L2-input error / redirect to parent" rule.**

## CLI entry points

Two flags:
- `--project "<name|id>"` → 1 Gantt for that project (wrapper, sub-project, or normal L1)
- `--client "<name|id>"` → N Gantts, one per top-level project (`parentProjectId IS NULL`) under the client. Renders each project through the full pipeline, writes one file per project, prints absolute paths and a summary line per Gantt.

## Constraints (operator-locked)

- `.tsx` component → HTML via `renderToStaticMarkup` from `react-dom/server`
- Issue detection deterministic and pure (no LLM)
- Implement only the rules below — no inventing extra rules or "section groupings"
- Sort rows by `startDate` ascending, **nulls last**. Title rendered verbatim from DB
- Header date range = raw entity dates (`null – null` if both null) — never derived from children
- Output: `~/runway-gantts/[client-slug]-[project-slug]-[YYYY-MM-DD].html`
- Stop and report after each wave. No PR pipeline.

## Header date format

`4/17 – 5/11` — numeric month, no zero-pad, no year, en-dash separator. Match row format. (Drop `Apr 17 – May 11`.)

## Reusable infrastructure

- DB connection: `createRunwayDb()` from `scripts/lib/run-script.ts`
- Env loading: `loadEnvLocal()` (auto-runs on import of `run-script.ts`)
- Direct-execution guard: `runIfDirect(name, fn)` from `scripts/lib/run-script.ts`
- Fuzzy match: `fuzzyMatch<T>` and `resolveEntityOrFail<T>` in `src/lib/runway/operations-utils.ts:189-276`
- Schemas: `projects` and `weekItems` in `src/lib/db/runway-schema.ts:26-94`
- Vitest config: `vitest.config.mts` — `happy-dom`, `@vitejs/plugin-react`, includes `**/*.test.{ts,tsx}`

`react`/`react-dom` 19.2.3 already in `package.json`. No new deps. Inline a tiny slugify (no exported util in scope).

## Files to create

```
scripts/
  runway-gantt.tsx                      # CLI entry point
  runway-gantt.test.ts                  # arg parsing, output path, --client fan-out
  lib/gantt/
    types.ts                            # Issue codes, GanttRow, RawData (discriminated union), GanttData
    resolve-entity.ts                   # fuzzy resolve + classify (wrapper/L1)
    resolve-entity.test.ts
    extract-data.ts                     # DB queries (children = projects OR weekItems based on view)
    extract-data.test.ts
    transform-rows.ts                   # children → GanttRow, sort, axis params, header range
    transform-rows.test.ts
    detect-issues.ts                    # L1, wrapper, child-project (wrapper view), weekItem (L1 view) detectors
    detect-issues.test.ts
    counter.ts                          # row-gap count + chart-issue count + itemized breakdown
    counter.test.ts
    GanttTemplate.tsx                   # React component: header + counter + alerts + body
    GanttTemplate.test.tsx              # rendered-HTML structural assertions
```

All `.ts` except `GanttTemplate.tsx` and the CLI entry, which contain JSX (Turbopack `.tsx`-for-JSX gotcha in `.claude/MEMORY.md`).

## Pre-work (before Wave 1)

Add to `package.json`:
```json
"runway:gantt": "npx tsx scripts/runway-gantt.tsx"
```

`scripts/lib/run-script.ts` calls `loadEnvLocal()` on import — same wiring as `runway:migrate` and `runway:publish-updates`.

## Wave 1 — Entity resolution

**Deliverable:** `scripts/lib/gantt/resolve-entity.ts` + tests.

**Behavior:**
1. Two inputs at the resolution layer: project name/id OR client name/id (CLI passes one or the other through).
2. **Project resolution**: if input matches a `projects.id` exactly → return that project; otherwise fuzzy-match across all projects on `name` (and `client.name + " / " + name` as a secondary key). Disambiguation list = `"<Client>: <Project Name>"`.
3. **Client resolution** (for `--client`): exact `clients.id` OR `clients.slug` first; otherwise fuzzy-match on `clients.name`. Same ambiguous/none handling pattern.
4. **Classify resolved project**:
   - Pull child projects (`WHERE parent_project_id = ?`) once.
   - `parentProjectId === null && engagementType === "retainer" && childProjects.length > 0` → `{ kind: "wrapper", project, childProjects }`
   - Else → `{ kind: "l1", project }` (weekItem children fetched in Wave 2)
5. For `--client`, return `{ kind: "client", client, topLevelProjects }` where `topLevelProjects = projects WHERE clientId = ? AND parentProjectId IS NULL`.

**Tests:** ambiguous-name disambiguation, wrapper detection (each of 3 conditions flipped), retainer-with-no-children → L1 view, sub-project (parentProjectId set) → L1 view (no error), id-input bypasses fuzzy match, client lookup by slug + name + id, client with zero top-level projects.

**Mechanical checks:** `pnpm test:run`, `pnpm lint`, live-DB sanity for `"AG1"`, `"AG1 PRO Content"` (sub-project), `"HDL Website Build"`, `"Convergix"`, `"Soundly Payment Gateway"`, and `--client "ag1"`.

## Wave 2 — Data extraction

**Deliverable:** `scripts/lib/gantt/extract-data.ts` + tests.

**Behavior:**
1. **Wrapper view**: children = the child L1 projects already loaded in Wave 1.
2. **L1 view**: children = `SELECT * FROM week_items WHERE project_id = ?` for the resolved project's id. Sort by `startDate` (Wave 3 handles this).
3. Look up the parent client row (for `client.name` + `client.slug`).
4. For wrapper-view children that are themselves L1s, also pull their startDate/endDate and contractStart/contractEnd to support `wrapper-range-misses-children` and `wrapper-child-contract-mismatch` detectors.
5. For L1-view, pull the parent project's startDate/endDate to support `wi-outside-parent-range`.
6. Return a discriminated union: `RawData = { kind: "wrapper", entity, client, children: ProjectRow[] } | { kind: "l1", entity, client, children: WeekItemRow[] }`.

**Tests:** wrapper with N child L1s, L1 with 0 weekItems, L1 with N weekItems, sub-project (parentProjectId !== null) returns its own weekItems, batch fetch shape (no N+1).

**Mechanical checks:** lint + tests + live-DB run on AG1 (wrapper, expect ≥1 child L1), AG1 PRO Content (sub-project, expect weekItems), HDL Website Build (L1 with weekItems).

## Wave 3 — Row transformation + axis params

**Deliverable:** `scripts/lib/gantt/transform-rows.ts` + tests.

**Behavior:**
1. Map each child to `GanttRow`. Discriminated:
   - **Wrapper-view row** (child = project): `{ kind: "project", id, title (= project.name), owner, resources, status, category, engagementType, parentProjectId, startDate, endDate, contractStart, contractEnd, dueDate, waitingOn }`
   - **L1-view row** (child = weekItem): `{ kind: "weekitem", id, title, owner, resources, status, category, startDate, endDate, weekOf }`
2. Sort by `startDate` ascending, **nulls last** (`null` → `+Infinity`).
3. Axis params: collect non-null start/end across rows + entity. All-null → `{ kind: "no-axis" }`. Span < 16 weeks → weekly columns. Else monthly. Carry `today: ISOString` for the today line.
4. Header range formatter: `4/17 – 5/11` numeric, no year, en-dash. `null – null` if both null. Single-date row (start === end) renders as `4/17`.
5. WeekItem with only `weekOf` set (no `startDate`/`endDate`) — do NOT synthesize from `weekOf`. Treat both dates as null. Surfaces the gap as red `null – null` per operator §9.

**Tests:** sort with mixed nulls, weekly/monthly threshold (15/17 weeks), all-null axis, header-range formatter for null permutations + same-day, weekItem with only weekOf renders as null/null.

**Mechanical checks:** lint + tests.

## Wave 4 — Issue detection

**Deliverable:** `scripts/lib/gantt/detect-issues.ts` + tests. Pure functions, no DB, no I/O.

### Issue codes

**Chart-level — L1 (chart subject is L1 or sub-project)**
- `l1-null-dates`, `l1-retainer-null-contract`, `l1-null-engagement-type`, `l1-null-category-or-status`, `l1-awaiting-null-waiting-on`, `l1-due-end-mismatch`, `l1-no-weekitems-no-owner`

**Chart-level — Wrapper (chart subject is wrapper)**
- `wrapper-null-contract`, `wrapper-no-children`, `wrapper-range-misses-children`, `wrapper-bad-engagement-type`, `wrapper-child-contract-mismatch`

**Row-level — wrapper view rows (deliverable L1 projects)**
- Inline (visualized in the row, not as sub-row alert): `row-both-dates-null`, `row-only-start-null`, `row-only-end-null`, `row-end-before-start`
- Sub-row alerts: `child-active-null-owner`, `child-orphan`, `child-parent-date-mismatch`, `child-end-before-start`, `child-status-category-mismatch`, `child-awaiting-null-waiting-on`, `child-null-engagement-when-parent-set`

**Row-level — L1 view rows (weekItems)**
- Inline: `wi-both-dates-null`, `wi-only-start-null`, `wi-only-end-null`, `wi-end-before-start`
- Sub-row alerts:
  - `wi-active-null-owner` — owner field exists on weekItem AND `status ∈ {in-progress, scheduled, at-risk}` (treating null as `scheduled`) AND `owner === null`
  - `wi-overdue` — `endDate < today` AND `status ∉ {completed, canceled}`
  - `wi-outside-parent-range` — weekItem range falls outside parent L1's `startDate`/`endDate`. Only fires if parent has BOTH dates.

WeekItems do NOT have `engagementType`, `contractStart/End`, or category-status mismatch — do not invent rules for fields that don't exist. Drop `wi-blocked-null-waiting-on` (waitingOn is project-only).

### Schema-enum source of truth (operator-confirmed)

Validator-enforced (alert on unexpected value):
- L1 `engagementType`: `retainer`, `project`. Schema comment lists `break-fix` but the validator rejects it — treat as invalid.
- L2 `category`: `delivery`, `review`, `kickoff`, `deadline`, `approval`, `launch`
- L2 `status`: `scheduled`, `in-progress`, `blocked`, `at-risk`, `completed`, `canceled` (null = treated as `scheduled`)

Free-form (alert only on null/empty, never "unexpected value"):
- L1 `category`: `active`, `awaiting-client`, `pipeline`, `on-hold`, `completed`
- L1 `status`: `in-production`, `awaiting-client`, `not-started`, `blocked`, `on-hold`, `completed`

### Module shape

Each detector returns `{ inline: Issue[]; subRow: Issue[] }` for row-level, or `Issue[]` for chart-level. `Issue = { code: IssueCode; message: string }`. Wrapper view selects between `detectChildProjectIssues` per row; L1 view selects `detectWeekItemIssues` per row.

**Tests:** one positive + one negative per code. Combined cases (e.g., weekItem with `wi-end-before-start` AND `wi-active-null-owner` — first inline, second sub-row). WeekItem-shaped fixtures for every wi-* rule. Project-shaped fixtures kept for wrapper-view rules. Exact-message assertions for any rule whose wording matters in the alert taxonomy.

**Mechanical checks:** lint + tests + live-DB sanity against AG1 wrapper, AG1 children, AG1 "Social Content Trial", AG1 PRO Content sub-project. Stop condition: if a real record fires a rule that operator says is wrong → report, don't silently change the rule.

## Wave 5 — React template

**Deliverable:** `scripts/lib/gantt/GanttTemplate.tsx` + tests.

**Component:** `<GanttTemplate data={GanttData} />` returning a complete `<html><head><style>...</style></head><body>...</body></html>` — single self-contained file.

**Render order (top to bottom):**
1. **Header**: project/wrapper name, raw date range (`4/17 – 5/11` or `null – null`), `Generated YYYY-MM-DD`, legend (active bar, setup bar, milestone glyph, alert badge)
2. **Counter line**: `"3 of 7 rows have data gaps + 2 chart-level issues"` (split counts; do not sum)
3. **Counter itemized breakdown**: list grouped by issue code with the affected entities
4. **Alert section**: chart-level alerts (L1 or wrapper, depending on subject) — also shown here in full alongside the counter breakdown (operator wants them in BOTH places)
5. **Gantt body** — table/grid layout (not SVG):
   - Each row: `title • O: <owner> · CD: Lane, CW: Kathy • inline-dates • bar/marker on timeline`
   - Bar = positioned `div` with `left/width` from axis params
   - Milestone (start === end) → CSS-rotated diamond glyph at the date
   - Today line = absolutely-positioned vertical div
   - Sub-row appears beneath the row IFF `subRow.length > 0` — small, indented, alert-colored
   - **Completed weekItem** (`status === "completed"`) → bar + text rendered with faded color treatment (e.g., 50% opacity), still visible
   - **Canceled weekItem** (`status === "canceled"`) → bar + text rendered with strikethrough + faded
6. `axis.kind === "no-axis"` → omit timeline column; rows still render with inline dates + sub-row alerts

**Render entry:** `renderGantt(data: GanttData): string` returning `"<!doctype html>" + renderToStaticMarkup(<GanttTemplate data={data} />)`.

**Tests:** structural assertions (parse via `happy-dom` `DOMParser` or substring/regex). Validate: header text and date format, row count, milestone diamond on same-day rows, no `.bar` element when both dates null, sub-row only when expected, today line presence/absence, completed faded class, canceled strikethrough class, counter line shows split counts, alert section also rendered below.

**Mechanical checks:** lint + tests. **Visual smoke**: open the rendered HTML in a browser before declaring the wave done (handoff requirement).

## Wave 6 — Counter + console mirror

**Deliverable:** `scripts/lib/gantt/counter.ts` + tests.

**Behavior:**
1. `summarize(data: GanttData): Summary` →
   ```
   {
     rowsWithGaps: number;       // count of rows where inline.length + subRow.length > 0
     totalRows: number;
     chartIssueCount: number;    // L1 or wrapper alerts (whichever applies to the subject)
     byCode: Record<IssueCode, RowRef[]>;
   }
   ```
   Counts are independent — never sum row-gap and chart-issue counts.
2. `formatCounterMarkup(summary)` → JSX for the template's counter slot. Format:
   - Headline: `"3 of 7 rows have data gaps + 2 chart-level issues"` (omit a side if zero — `"0 chart-level issues"` is ugly; render `"3 of 7 rows have data gaps"` alone).
   - Itemized list grouped by code with friendly labels (e.g., `"3 children missing end date: A, B, C"`). Sort codes alphabetically for stability.
3. `formatCounterConsole(summary, outputPath)` → plain-text version: headline + itemized breakdown + the absolute output path on the final line.

**Tests:** zero issues → `"0 of N rows have data gaps"`, zero chart issues → no chart-level clause, grouping logic, deterministic ordering, console output includes path.

**Mechanical checks:** lint + tests.

## Wave 7 — CLI wrapper

**Deliverable:** `scripts/runway-gantt.tsx` + `scripts/runway-gantt.test.ts`.

**Behavior:**
1. Args: `--project <name|id>` XOR `--client <name|id>`. Reject if both or neither present (usage to stderr, `exit(1)`).
2. **`--project` path**: resolve → extract → transform → detect → summarize → render → write. Print console mirror (with absolute output path).
3. **`--client` path**: resolve client → fetch top-level projects (`parentProjectId IS NULL`) for that client → for each: run the full project pipeline, write a separate file, print one console-mirror block per Gantt. Final summary line: `Wrote N Gantts for <Client>` + bullet list of paths.
4. Output path: `path.join(os.homedir(), "runway-gantts", `${slugify(client.name)}-${slugify(project.name)}-${YYYY-MM-DD}.html`)`. `mkdirSync(dir, { recursive: true })`. `writeFileSync(path, html, "utf-8")`. Inline 5-line slugify (`toLowerCase`, replace `[^a-z0-9]+` with `-`, strip leading/trailing `-`).
5. Errors: try/catch the pipeline. Turso connection errors → hint at `RUNWAY_DATABASE_URL` env var. Resolution failures (no match / ambiguous) → print disambiguation list. Sub-project input renders normally (no error).

**Tests:** arg parsing (missing/both/valid), `--client` with N projects → N writes (mock the pipeline), output-path slug correctness for names with punctuation/spaces, error-message wording for ambiguous matches.

**Mechanical checks:** lint + tests. **End-to-end smoke**: `pnpm runway:gantt --project "AG1"` → file written, opens in browser, header reads "AG1" + raw date range, alerts populated. Then `pnpm runway:gantt --client "ag1"` → multiple files written.

## Wave 8 — Cross-project validation

**Deliverable:** observation report back to operator. Iterate template/thresholds based on findings; do not silently change rules.

**Required runs:**
- AG1 wrapper (worst case, with Social Content Trial)
- AG1 PRO Content sub-project (renders weekItems, currently has 1)
- HDL Website Build (non-retainer L1, renders weekItems)
- Convergix wrapper
- Soundly Payment Gateway (non-retainer L1)
- L1 with zero weekItems (degenerate — find one in DB)
- Invalid input (non-existent project name → fuzzy-match disambiguation message)

**For each run**: open rendered HTML in browser. Capture observations against spec. Report any rule firing that looks wrong, or any visual issue, before changing thresholds.

**Tests woven in**: add fixture-based regression tests in `detect-issues.test.ts` for any genuine surprises uncovered.

**Mechanical checks:** `pnpm test:run` + `pnpm lint` green at the end. Operator review gate before any commit. No PR.

## Verification (end-to-end)

After Wave 7, before Wave 8:
1. `pnpm test:run` — all green
2. `pnpm lint` — zero errors
3. `pnpm runway:gantt --project "AG1"` — exits 0, writes file, prints absolute path + counter mirror
4. Open the file — header `4/17 – 5/11` (or actual numeric range), counter line splits row vs chart counts, alert section also present below, rows visible, today line drawn
5. `pnpm runway:gantt --project "AG1 PRO Content"` (sub-project) — renders normally with its weekItems; no error
6. `pnpm runway:gantt --client "ag1"` — writes multiple files, prints all paths
7. `pnpm runway:gantt --project "Nonexistent"` — exits 1 with disambiguation/none message

## Stop conditions (per handoff)

- Pre-plan ambiguity surfaces during implementation
- A data-quality rule fires on a record that operator says is fine
- AG1 (or any test fixture) renders something that looks wrong
- Turso/env/connection issues block reading data
- Each wave completion (built-in checkpoint)

## Out of scope (do not drift)

- PNG / Playwright (Phase 2)
- Slack triggering (Phase 1B)
- Brand polish (R2)
- Caching, hosted live URL, Google Drive output, multi-format bundle, AI-generated text
- Modifying project titles, deriving header dates from children, inventing sections
- Editing the pre-plan file (TP owns that)

# Account View — Gantt Pre-Plan (2026-04-30) ## Context The local Gantt CLI shipped Phase 1A: `pnpm runway:gantt --project|--client` renders an HTML Gantt with a Data Integrity panel, status-aware bar coloring (in-progress/scheduled/at-risk/blocked/completed/canceled), milestone diamonds, today line, daily gridlines, Monday+Thursday axis ticks, and (for `--client`) a single-page rundown with per-client severity rollup, table-of-contents card grid, and per-child rollup. All 178 tests green, 0 lint errors. Branch: `feature/gantt-cli`. Worktree: `.worktrees/gantt-cli/`. **Goal of this work:** port the Gantt visual language into Runway's Account View tab (dark mode), so each client card on `/runway` Account tab renders an inline rundown of its projects. The data-integrity Rundown + project Triage Gantts we built remain unchanged — they stay light-themed and continue to be triggered by Slack command or Claude Code session, not by the Account view. **Operator-locked constraints:** - Runway is dark-mode-only for now. Don't try to retheme Runway. - No data integrity panel, no per-row sub-row alerts on the Account view. Triage stays out. - One bridge from Account view to triage: a small lazy-loaded "Audit" badge per client card that signals "go run a rundown locally to see why." - Click-to-expand at every layer (client, project section), default everything open, alphabetical clients. - The current right-hand Flags column on the Account view goes away (Week View covers it). - No JS-heavy expand/collapse — native `
`/``. ## Architecture summary ``` Account View (dark, /runway "By Account" tab) ├── Hide existing right-hand "Flags" column ├── For each client (alphabetical): │
← client card │ ├── Summary: client name · contract dates · [Audit badge, Suspense] │ └── Inline rundown body (no header chrome) │ └── For each project section (alphabetical, empty L1s last): │
← project section │ ├── Summary: project name · status pill · date range │ └── Gantt body (rows + axis + today line, no data integrity panel) Rundown + Triage Gantts (light, ~/runway-gantts/*.html) └── UNCHANGED. Triggered only by `pnpm runway:gantt` or Slack command. ``` The same pure detector/summary code feeds both views. The Account view consumes only the severity rollup (for the badge) and the row/axis data (for visual gantt). It does not render the Data Integrity panel or per-row sub-rows. ## Phases Each phase is a checkpoint.
